description:
WHAT: One call per batch of leads/counterparties: runs email_validate_deliverability on their emails and sanctions_screen_names on their person/company names IN PARALLEL, then merges results per lead with an overall decision: block (invalid email or sanctions potential_match), review (risky email), pass.
WHEN: Onboarding customers/vendors, qualifying inbound leads, CRM hygiene where both email quality and sanctions exposure matter.
WHEN NOT: Email only -> email_validate_deliverability; names only -> sanctions_screen_names (same per-item prices, no merge step). Free pre-filter first: email_check_syntax. Use this tool only when a lead needs both checks and one decision.
COST: Paid, billed to YOUR Apify account via your APIFY_TOKEN: $0.00079 per lead with email + $0.003 per lead with name (= $0.00379 per full lead) + $0.007 per call for the sanctions run. 100 full leads ~ $0.39.
RETURNS: Paged "lead" rows (decision pass | review | block with reasons[]; sanctions_matches holds the top 3); meta.summary counts by decision. Partial failure: the affected check shows "unavailable" and meta.errors lists codes. Tool errors: INPUT_EMPTY, APIFY_TOKEN_MISSING.
BEHAVIOR: No email is sent. Runs the email and sanctions Apify Actors in parallel (2 runs per call) in your account; ~5-45 s (sanctions lists come from a cache at most 6 h old, or are downloaded), 300 s timeout.
PARAMETERS: leads: each record needs email and/or name (if no lead has either -> INPUT_EMPTY, nothing billed); a lead with only an email skips sanctions (sanctions_status "not_checked") and one with only a name skips email (email_verdict "not_checked"), so a lead is billed for each check it gets (prices under COST), plus the per-call sanctions run fee when any lead has a name. Identical emails across leads are validated and billed once. ref joins sanctions results back to the lead, so keep refs unique (default = the lead's 0-based index as a string). country and entityType apply to that lead's sanctions check only: entityType filters candidates, while country only annotates matches (never removes them). minScore: sanctions similarity threshold; default 88 here (stricter than the 85 of sanctions_screen_names) to keep block decisions low-noise; each name returns at most its top 3 matches. allowFreeProviders=false turns gmail.com-type addresses into email_verdict "risky", i.e. decision "review" (never "block"). Decision precedence: any sanctions potential_match or invalid email -> block; else risky email or an incomplete check -> review; else pass. limit/offset page the merged lead rows, but every call re-runs and re-bills both checks for all leads (also when only offset changes), so set limit (max 1000) to cover all leads; meta.summary counts all leads.
EXAMPLE: {"leads":[{"ref":"L1","email":"cfo@acme.com","name":"Acme Trading LLC","country":"US"}]} -> {decision:"pass",email_verdict:"valid",sanctions_status:"no_match"}

allowFreeProviders.description: Optional boolean, default true. false makes free webmail (gmail.com, outlook.com, ...) email_verdict "risky" -> decision "review"; recommended for B2B

leads.description: Required. 1-1000 lead objects {ref?, email?, name?, country?, entityType?}; each needs email and/or name. Example: [{"ref":"L1","email":"cfo@acme.com","name":"Acme Trading LLC","country":"US","entityType":"entity"}]

country.description: Optional, <= 60 chars. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code ("US") or English country name; sets country_match on sanctions matches, does not filter

email.description: Optional (email and/or name required), <= 320 chars. One email address, e.g. "cfo@acme.com"; "Name <addr>" accepted

entityType.description: Optional, one of "individual" | "entity" | "any", default "any". Restricts sanctions candidates for this lead's name

name.description: Optional (email and/or name required), <= 300 chars. Person or company name to sanctions-screen, e.g. "Acme Trading LLC"

ref.description: Optional, <= 200 chars, must be unique per call. Your ID echoed back as ref, e.g. "crm-123"; default = the lead's 0-based index as a string ("0", "1", ...)

limit.description: Optional page size: items to return, integer 1-1000 (default 100). Example: 50

minScore.description: Optional integer 60-100, default 88. Minimum 0-100 fuzzy name-similarity for a sanctions potential_match (which blocks the lead). Example: 92

offset.description: Optional zero-based number of items to skip, integer 0-1000000 (default 0); pass nextOffset from the previous response, e.g. 100

name: trust_screen_lead

count.description: Number of items in this page

hasMore.description: True if more items exist after this page

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page, or null

offset.description: Offset of the first item in this page

title: Screen leads: email deliverability + sanctions (paid)
